text:
ivy: Ran into a weird chain today while onboarding a partner. Installer one-liner fails behind their corporate proxy (TLS intercept) and `redwoodctl login --browser=none` returns a device code that later fails with `invalid_verification_code`.

noah: corp proxies are common cause. Did the browser flow from the host machine work? WSL/git-bash flows often hit redirect issues.

ivy: browser on host worked, but copying the profile into the dev VM produced a merged config with duplicated `profiles:` keys and redwoodctl ignored the imported profile.

carla: we've seen two separate bugs: 1) installer will naively append user config to existing global config if REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH is set -> duplicate keys. 2) device-code verification had a race on nonce validation for some OS clocks leading to `invalid_verification_code`. Both are being tracked.

ivy: any short workarounds so partner can continue testing?

noah: quick steps that worked for me: 1) do `redwoodctl login` on a machine with working browser 2) copy the exact profile YAML block from ~/.redwood/config.yaml 3) on the target VM write an explicit config with that block and set `current_profile: <name>` (don't concatenate files). Example snippet: `mkdir -p ~/.redwood && cat > ~/.redwood/config.yaml <<'YAML'
profiles:
  partner:
    token: "<paste>"
current_profile: partner
YAML`

carla: also `redwoodctl login --output-token` exists but is undocumented in some versions; it prints a raw token you can set as REDWOOD_TOKEN in the target env. That avoids file merging entirely.

ivy: used `--output-token` and set REDWOOD_TOKEN in the VM env, local serve now picks it up. thanks. :tada:

auth-bot: NOTE: auth service observed transient 400s for device-code verify between 2025-11-03T14:00 and 14:20 UTC; retry/backoff fix backported to master (PR #2217).

carla: follow-ups: we'll 1) make installer respect REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH properly (avoid naive append), 2) add an explicit `redwoodctl profiles import --from <path> --set-current <name>` that validates merges, and 3) expose a supported `--headless` flag for WSL/CI flows that prints token and handles retries. Filed DX-645, DX-646, DX-647.

noah: small note about UX: when `current_profile` is missing the CLI defaults silently which confuses new users. I suggest `profiles import` auto-select the first profile if `current_profile` is unset unless `--no-select` is passed.

carla: agreed. adding to DX-646. Also adding `redwoodctl doctor` to print effective config paths (checked: /etc/redwood, $REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH, ~/.redwood, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME) and any conflicts.

ivy: two more gotchas I hit: 1) our CI baked configs into images and stale tokens are common; we switched to injecting REDWOOD_TOKEN in runtime which fixed it. 2) YAML anchors in partner-provided config broke the importer (merge key unsupported). I had to expand anchors with `yq` before importing.

noah: for CI patterns, prefer `redwoodctl profiles import --from-stdin` or env var approach. I'll add a small entrypoint script template to devex/cli/ci.md.

docs-bot: draft PR created devex/cli/install-and-auth.md covering proxy troubleshooting, headless flows, REDWOOD_CONFIG_PATH precedence, and CI patterns.

ivy: thanks all. Once the headless flag lands and installer avoids appending global configs this will be much smoother for partners. Closing the loop for now — will re-open if partner hits more issues. :white_check_mark:
